chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Bistam ibn Murra from Is'haq ibn Hassan from Haytham ibn Waqid from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Abdi from Abu Harun from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he was asked: 'What is your opinion regarding this fish which our brethren from the people of Kufa allege is prohibited?'

So Abu Sa'id said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: Kufa is the skull of the Arabs, and the spear of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and a treasure of faith, so take from them. I inform you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stayed in Mecca for a day and a night, hungry. Then he went out and I went out with him. We passed by a group sitting and eating lunch. They said: O Messenger of Allah, the lunch! He said to them: Yes, make way for your Prophet. So he sat between two men, and I sat, and he took a loaf and broke it in half. Then he looked at their sauce and said: What is this sauce of yours? They said: The sea bass, O Messenger of Allah. So he threw the piece from his hand and arose.'

Abu Sa'id said: 'And I stayed behind after him to see what the people's opinion was. The people differed among themselves. A group said: The Messenger of Allah prohibited the sea bass. And a group said: He did not prohibit it, but excused himself from it. For if he had prohibited it, he would have forbidden us from eating it. So I memorized their discussion and followed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) trotting until I caught up with him.'

Then we came to another group eating lunch. They said: O Messenger of Allah, the lunch! He said: Yes, make way for your Prophet. So he sat between two men, and I sat with him. When he took a piece, he looked at the sauce of the people and said: What is this sauce of yours? They said: Lizard, O Messenger of Allah. So he threw the piece and arose.

Abu Sa'id said: 'So I stayed behind afterwards, and the people were in two groups. One group said: The Messenger of Allah prohibited it, so from there they did not eat it. And another group said: He only excused himself from it. And if he had prohibited it, he would have forbidden us from eating it. Then I followed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) until I caught up with him.'

So we passed by the base of Safa, and there were pots boiling. They said: O Messenger of Allah, if you would stop by us until our pots are ready. He said to them: What is in your pots? They said: Donkeys of ours that we were riding, they stalled, so we slaughtered them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) approached the pots and overturned them with his foot. Then he went away trotting, and I stayed behind. Some of them said: The Messenger of Allah prohibited the flesh of donkeys. And some said: No, he only emptied your pots so that you would not return and slaughter your beasts.

Abu Sa'id said: 'So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent for me. When I came to him, he said: O Abu Sa'id, call Bilal for me. When I brought Bilal to him, he said: O Bilal, ascend Abu Qubays and call out that the Messenger of Allah has prohibited the sea bass, the lizard, and the domesticated donkeys. Indeed, fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not eat from the fish except what has a peel, and with the peel being scales.'
For indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, transformed seven hundred communities who disobeyed the Successors after the Messengers, so He took four hundred of them by land and three hundred by sea.
So We made them a tale and scattered them all around.

key_terms.الْجِرِّيثُ: Sea bass or a specific type of fish

ai.seo_question: What specific animals did the Prophet Muhammad prohibit eating according to the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the jurisprudential distinction between *karaahat* (dislike/preference) and *haram* (prohibition) by contrasting the Prophet's initial silent rejection of *al-jirith* and *al-dabb* with his explicit declaration of prohibition for domesticated donkeys. The narrative highlights the scholarly debate in Kufa regarding whether the Prophet's action constituted a binding legal ruling or merely a personal preference, ultimately resolved by Bilal's call confirming the prohibition. It further connects these dietary laws to the cosmic theme of divine transformation (*masakh*) as a consequence of disobedience to the Imams.
